payload.goal: Add expense categories to the splitter. Extend the Expense type with an optional category field validated against a fixed set of categories, add computeCategoryTotals to the domain, expose listCategoryTotals from the API layer, render a category breakdown in the web surface, and cover the new behaviour with tests. Preserve the existing balance behaviour and keep the current tests green.

acceptanceIntents.description: Expense supports an optional category field that is accepted only when it belongs to the fixed category set.
The domain layer exposes computeCategoryTotals and aggregates expenses by category correctly.
The API layer exposes listCategoryTotals backed by the domain category totals behavior.
The web summary surface renders a category breakdown from the category totals API data.
Existing balance behavior remains unchanged and current tests stay green.

root.title: Add expense category breakdown
root.objective: Add validated optional expense categories, category total computation, API exposure, web rendering, and tests while preserving existing balance behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Expenses can carry an optional validated category.
Category totals are computed independently from balance totals.
API consumers can request category totals.
The summary UI displays a category breakdown.
Existing balance tests and behavior remain intact.

cut.rationale: The change crosses domain, API, web rendering, and tests, with public type/API additions but no indicated persistence or external integration.

children.title: Add validated category field
children.objective: Extend the Expense model with an optional category constrained to a fixed category set and cover valid, missing, and invalid category cases.
expectedOutcomes: Expense includes an optional category field.
The fixed category set is represented in the domain layer.
Invalid category values are rejected at the same boundary where expenses are validated or constructed.
Existing expenses without a category remain valid.

children.title: Compute category totals
children.objective: Add computeCategoryTotals in the domain layer and verify totals aggregate by category without changing balance calculations.
expectedOutcomes: computeCategoryTotals returns totals grouped by category.
Uncategorized expenses have deterministic handling in the returned totals.
Existing balance computation behavior remains unchanged.
Domain tests cover multiple categories, repeated categories, and balance regression.

children.title: Expose category totals API
children.objective: Expose listCategoryTotals from the API layer using the domain category totals behavior and cover the API contract with tests.
expectedOutcomes: The API function delegates category aggregation to the domain behavior instead of duplicating aggregation rules.
API tests verify the returned category totals shape and values.

children.title: Render category breakdown
children.objective: Render category totals in the web summary surface and verify the existing balance summary remains available.
expectedOutcomes: src/web/summary.ts renders category totals as a category breakdown.
The web surface continues to render the existing balance summary behavior.
Web summary tests cover populated category totals and balance-preservation behavior.

uncertainties.description: The goal does not specify whether expenses without a category should be omitted from category totals or grouped under an uncategorized bucket.
uncertainties.impact: This changes observable totals and UI rendering, but the optional category requirement allows an implementer to choose the smallest behavior consistent with existing patterns if repository inspection reveals one.

uncertainties.description: The goal requires a fixed set of categories but does not list the category names.
uncertainties.impact: The exact allowed values affect tests and displayed labels. Repository inspection may reveal naming conventions; otherwise the implementer should choose a small explicit set and keep it centralized.
